notes: Play knowledge rewritten as executable actions. Every reference is checked against the generated level data by tools/gen_level_nuance.py.
Surface 2 reuses Surface 1's terrain at night. The map knowledge transfers; the threat model does not, because visibility is far worse and the sniper rifle is gone.

nuance.claim: The terrain is the same compound as Surface 1, so routes learned there transfer directly even though the objectives differ.
nuance.because: Both levels resolve to the same navigation graph size, 251 nodes, and the guides describe it as the same map at night.

nuance.claim: There is no sniper rifle here, so the long-range approach that works on Surface 1 is unavailable and engagements happen at much shorter range.
Ammunition is scarce on higher difficulties, so shots are taken deliberately rather than sprayed; running dry mid-compound is a common failure.
The night sky cuts visibility badly, so guards are heard or run into rather than seen at distance; movement should assume contact at any moment.
The surveillance equipment is several separate targets scattered around the compound, so it is cleared while moving between other objectives rather than as one trip.
nuance.because: Objective 0 names four separate destroy tags.

nuance.claim: Cameras sit on the outside of the cabin that held the large key in Surface 1 and on the catwalks of the dish tower, both of which are passed anyway.
Breaking the communications link means destroying more than one target, so the objective is not complete after the first.
Entering the bunker ends the level, so it is left until the surveillance, communications and aircraft objectives are all done.
nuance.because: Objective 3 is the level exit; anything unfinished scores as failed.

nuance.claim: Because the map is shared, the reliable way to handle the darkness is to know the layout in advance rather than to navigate by sight.
